errors.problem: 'Today is Thursday' is a nominal sentence whose subject should be nominative: الْيَوْمُ الْخَمِيسُ. With fatḥa, الْيَوْمَ is the adverb 'today' (as it correctly is in الْيَوْمَ لَا نَقْرَأُ), so the sentence has no subject. The seg gloss 'today' hides the problem.
errors.alsoChange: segs[2] gloss → 'the day ('today', subject)'; transliteration follows (Al-yawmu l-khamīs)

errors.problem: Tap gloss in أَعْرِفُ أَنَّهَا تُحِبُّ الْمُوسِيقَى: the subject is 'she' (annahā), so تُحِبُّ is 'she loves/likes'. The tap shows the masculine-you sense from another sentence.

Tap gloss belongs to another sentence (predicate of kāna). Here عُطْلَةً is the direct object of أَعْلَنَتْ, which is why it ends in -an. In the same taps أَعْلَنَ=announces (past) is self-contradictory (should be '(he) announced').

In Day 75 every إِنَّهَا is reported speech after قَالَتْ ('that she'), but the tap gloss is the Day 73 sense 'indeed it (f) (it is)'. The seg of d75s2 correctly says 'that she (after qāla)'; the taps on the same word contradict it, including on the correct quiz answer.

errors.current: أَنْتَ=you (written without vowel marks: anta or anti)
errors.problem: The quiz word is fully vocalised أَنْتَ (anta, to a man); the tap gloss says it is written without vowel marks and could be anti, which is false here and confuses the gender lesson of the week.

حِمَايَةُ is the maṣdar 'protecting, protection (of)'; glossing it with the finite verb 'protects' contradicts the lesson point that it is a verbal noun (the seg in d78l14 has it right: 'protecting, protection (of)').

The 'wrong' form is correct MSA when addressing a woman (jussive 2 f. sg. of أَعْطَى is تُعْطِي: لَا تُعْطِي). The pair is only wrong for a man, and the why ('the long ī drops to a short i') states it as a general rule, so a learner will think لَا تُعْطِي is always an error.
errors.fix: keep the pair but make the why say: 'to a man, after لَا meaning don't, the final ī of تُعْطِي drops: lā tuʿṭi. To a woman the form is lā tuʿṭī.'
errors.alsoChange: tap تُعْطِي → 'you (m) give / she gives; don't give! (to a woman)'

errors.problem: Engine: the relative pronouns الَّذِي / الَّتِي / الَّذِينَ are transliterated 'Illadhī', 'illatī', 'illadhīna' whenever they stand alone or follow an unvowelled word (ʿIndī ṣadīq illadhī). The hamzat waṣl of al- is a-: alladhī, allatī, alladhīna. After a vowel the engine is right (ar-rajulu lladhī); only the relative pronouns are affected.
Engine: a final unvowelled yāʾ after a consonant (رَأْي) is transliterated as a long ī. The word is raʾy (one syllable, diphthong-like final y), as in shayʾ ≠ shāī. The Arabic is correct.

errors.problem: Engine: two definite-article sequences break the transliterator. (1) وَبِالْحَيَوَانَاتِ وَبِالْأَشْجَار → 'wabiālḥayawānāti wabiālʾashjār' instead of 'wa-bi-l-ḥayawānāti wa-bi-l-ashjār' (the chain wa- + bi- + al- is not elided). (2) الِاجْتِمَاعِيِّ (hamzat waṣl of اِجْتِمَاعِيّ written with kasra under the alif) → 'liājtimāʿiyyi' instead of 'l-ijtimāʿiyyi', in d79s3, both mistakes variants and d79l11. The Arabic is correct in all five places.

errors.fix: leave ة untransliterated in prose (or 'tāʾ marbūṭa')

errors.problem: Engine (known quirk): a name after the clitics وَ / لِ is capitalised as one word: 'Dānyāl Walaylā Wasāmī', 'laysa Likhālid', 'kitāb Linajīb Maḥfūẓ', 'abī Liʿumar', 'fī l-yawm Liʿumar'. Should be wa-Laylā wa-Sāmī, li-Khālid, li-Najīb, li-ʿUmar (compare the correct 'ʿUmar', 'Laylā' elsewhere).

notes.note: Indirect yes/no questions with هَلْ (سَأَلَنِي هَلْ فَهِمْتُ، سَأَلَنِي هَلْ لَيْلَى بِخَيْر) are common in modern journalistic MSA, but careful style prefers إِنْ كُنْتُ / إِذَا كَانَتْ or عَمَّا إِذَا. Not an error; a register choice worth knowing if the course later teaches إِذَا.

لَازِم أَنْ is colloquial-flavoured (Levantine/Egyptian lāzim); in written MSA the usual forms are يَجِبُ أَنْ, يَلْزَمُ أَنْ or مِنَ اللَّازِمِ أَنْ. The lesson presents it beside يَجِبُ أَنْ as equal MSA; consider labelling it 'everyday / spoken'.

notes.note: The tap gloss for إِنَّ is always 'that (after say)', even where the lesson teaches the sentence-initial sense 'indeed' (إِنَّ الْأَخْبَارَ جَيِّدَة). The segs say 'indeed' correctly; only the dictionary tap is one-sided. A two-sense gloss 'indeed; that (after qāla)' would fit both days.
Tap gloss مَنْ=who appears on every proverb, while the lesson's whole point is that مَنْ here means 'whoever'. Segs are right; the tap could read 'who?; whoever (in sayings)'.
Prose says خَاصّ (private) but the tap gloss says 'special'. Both are correct senses of خَاصّ; the tap could carry 'special; private, personal' to match مَعْلُومَاتِنَا الْخَاصَّة in d79l12.

حَتَّى أَبُوكُمَا (nominative) reads حَتَّى as 'even' opening a new clause, which is fine. If read as coordinating with لِأَيِّ شَخْصٍ it would be genitive أَبِيكُمَا. Either is defensible; no change needed.

إِنْ دَرَسْتَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ، نَجَحْتَ is the classical past–past conditional and is correct, but it is rarer in modern usage than إِنْ دَرَسْتَ … فَسَتَنْجَحُ / تَنْجَحْ; learners may find the fa- pattern taught in d80s1 more consistent.
خَمْسَ سَاعَاتٍ is the 3–10 number rule, but the grammar tag is numbers-11-100.
Tap كَثِيرٌ=many for مَالٌ كَثِيرٌ; 'much, a lot of' (as in the seg) fits an uncountable noun.

Mid-phrase words left without a final vowel (يَوْم مِثْل هٰذَا, شَيْء غَيْر حَقِيقِيّ) follow the course's everyday-dialogue style; the transliteration mirrors it (mithl hādhā). Consistent, so not reported, but formal readings would be مِثْلُ / غَيْرِ.
صَلَاة is transliterated Ṣalāh (pausal ة as h). Acceptable ALA-LC pausal form; elsewhere the engine drops the ة entirely (Ḥukūma, Jarīda). Minor inconsistency only.

summary: Read the whole export for days 71–80 (2,829 lines: festivals, music/film, headlines with إِنَّ, relative pronouns, reported speech, opinions, proverbs, environment, technology, conditionals). Checked every Arabic line for spelling, harakat, case after إِنَّ/أَنَّ/لٰكِنَّ/كَانَ/لَيْسَ, mood after أَنْ/لَنْ/لَمْ, agreement (non-human plurals, verb-first singular, dual), number–noun rules (ثَلَاثَ جَرَائِد, ثَلَاثَةَ أَخْبَار, عَشْرَ شَجَرَات, مِئَتَا جُنَيْهٍ), diptotes (عُمَرُ, غَضْبَانَ, أَشْيَاءَ), the English and literal translations, all seg and tap glosses, all 70 quiz answer keys and the mistakes pairs. The Arabic itself is very clean: the only case slip is الْيَوْمَ الْخَمِيس for 'today is Thursday'. The remaining findings are tap-gloss mismatches where a dictionary gloss from another sentence's sense is shown (تُحِبُّ, عُطْلَةً, إِنَّهَا, حِمَايَةُ, أَنْتَ), one mistakes pair that brands a form wrong which is correct for a woman (لَا تُعْطِي), and five engine quirks (الَّذِي → Illadhī, رَأْي → Raʾī, وَبِالْ/الِاجْتِمَاعِيّ chains, ة → 'A / at', clitic+name capitalisation). All quiz answer keys are correct. 0 major, 12 minor (7 content, 5 engine), 11 notes.
